text: Who actually checked this carbon credit?
A developer wrote the baseline. An auditor stamped it once. Then everyone moved on.
Here is how the industry works today.
The developer picks a reference region and a deforestation rate.
That one number decides how many credits exist. Nobody re-derives it from pixels.
Investigations found that more than ninety percent of some rainforest offsets were phantom.
Then the credit is sold, and resold, and nothing watches the forest.
On our Manavgat pilot area, one fire year removed one point two million tonnes of carbon. The registry never noticed.
And the ratings? A private model, a letter grade, and a request to trust it.
Three gaps. The baseline, the time, and the score.
VeriCanopy starts from the pixels, not the paperwork.
Every period, the oracle pulls Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, Hansen forest loss, GEDI biomass, MODIS burned area and Dynamic World.
For the project, and for a matched twin forest nearby.
Seven hundred seventy-six project pixels against two thousand four hundred twin pixels.
The twin is the counterfactual. The gap between the two curves is what the credit has to pay for.
Sixteen features feed a small, audited network of four hundred seventeen parameters.
Tapajós scored seventy-one point nine in 2023. After eight thousand tonnes of detected loss, three point nine.
But a score alone is just another number to trust. So the inference runs inside a zero-knowledge circuit.
Six seconds. A four-kilobyte proof.
The Halo2 verifier on Base Sepolia checks it before the score is stored. A wrong proof reverts the transaction.
This is the real transaction on Basescan. Anyone can open it.
And the evidence manifest is signed with ML-DSA-65, a post-quantum signature, so the record stays checkable for decades.
Now the credit itself changes.
When loss is detected, the buffer burns first.
A shortfall freezes the project, blocks transfers, and notifies every holder.
And anyone can challenge a score with a bond. Two of three independent resolvers recompute it.
This is live today. Let me use it.
The registry: every project on a map, with its live integrity status.
Open Tapajós. Real Sentinel-2 before and after, the twin chart, and the fire year.
Scrub the years, check the fire watch, open the leakage ring.
Proofs and signatures: the model hash, the manifest, the on-chain transaction, and a signed auditor report.
Verify it yourself: hash against chain, key against registry, signature, and proof.
Try to register land that overlaps an existing project. The contract refuses.
The market sells living credits with the score on the price tag.
Ask explains any score, feature by feature, with no language model in the loop.
And Status shows the whole stack breathing.
Agents can use it too. In Claude, I add the VeriCanopy connector.
Then I just ask.
Claude reads the registry, explains the score, and prepares a transaction that my wallet signs.
Pull back, and the whole picture is there. Pixels, a twin, a score, a proof, a chain, and a credit that keeps watching.
Ratings you must trust. Or proofs you can check.
VeriCanopy. Live on Base Sepolia. Open source.
